validity.recommendation: Treat as a probable overlap with P1485 (the Ananiv-Bohorodchany part of the same trunk). Do not merge or delete until a source gives the split. The 333 km length has no source.
validity.researcher_notes: Moldovatransgaz names this exact line (Ананьев - Черновцы - Богородчаны) with 1020 mm and 9.1 bcm/y, which match the sheet. The Ukrtransgaz chronology has no separate Ananiv-Bohorodchany pipeline. It lists one Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany line of 532.6 km and 1020 mm, whose compressor stations run Ananiv, Sholdanesti and Drochia (Moldova), Khotyn, Bohorodchany. That is the same corridor, and P1485 covers the whole line. The 333 km does not fit: Moldova section 184.8 km, and 532.6 minus 333 leaves 199.6 km for Kremenchuk to Ananiv, which is shorter than the straight-line distance of about 300 km. So the duplicate question stays open. I did not find a source that splits the line into P1485 and P1481. Other findings: Owner2 (Transgaz SA, Romania) has no support. The 1987 start year is not stated on any page naming this line.

fills.researcher_notes: Moldovatransgaz page "Main gas pipelines for gas transmission across Moldova" (dated 29 January 2021) lists "Ананьев - Черновцы - Богородчаны (АЧБ)" among 8 trunk lines it services: 184.8 km in Moldova, 1020 mm, 9.1 billion cubic meters a year, for Moldovan consumers. That supports Moldovatransgaz as operator of the Moldovan section. The Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine key facts page (2025 web archive capture; the live page blocks this machine) says it operates the Ukrainian trunk network but does not name this line. So the Ukrainian operator is supported only by that general statement.

No source found for either owner. The sheet spells Owner2 as SNTGN Transgaz SA, which is Romania's gas transmission company. The Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine key facts page does not name this line. Nothing found links Transgaz to a Ukraine-Moldova line, so Owner2 looks wrong. Searched Moldovatransgaz pages, Ukrainian and Russian web searches for the line name, and the Ukrtransgaz chronology. The Moldovan section is probably Moldovatransgaz-owned, but no page says so.

Moldovatransgaz gives only the Moldovan section, 184.8 km, not 333 km end to end. The Ukrtransgaz chronology gives 532.6 km for the whole Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany line and has no separate Ananiv-Bohorodchany entry. No source states 333 km. Searched Ukrainian and Russian line names plus the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine and Moldovatransgaz pages.

The Ukrtransgaz chronology (web archive capture) puts the Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany line in service in 1986 and lists its 532.6 km, 1020 mm entry under 1987. The Ananiv-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany corridor looks like part of that line, but no page names P1481 itself or states its own start year. The Moldovatransgaz page has no dates. So 1987 is consistent with the chronology but is not staged as a ref, because the page does not name this line.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated page that names the line is the Moldovatransgaz page from January 2021, which lists it as serviced. Nothing dated 2024 or later names it. The Moldova interconnection news from 2024 and 2025 covers the Trans-Balkan and Orlovka lines, not this one. Russian transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025, and this line carried Balkan-bound gas, so its present use is not documented. No status change is proposed. The Moldovan section is the one with evidence.
